title: Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages · Part 2
note: GENERATED by scripts/generate-part-two.mjs from the core lesson — do not hand-edit.
contentObjective: I can write equivalent fractions, decimals, and percents for the same value.
languageObjective: I can explain my conversions using the words percent, decimal, equivalent, and benchmark.

vocabulary.definition: Three equivalent ways to name the same part of a whole.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tres maneras equivalentes de nombrar la misma parte de un todo.
vocabulary.cloze: Three equivalent ways to name the same part of a whole are ___, ___ and ___.

examples.why: All three name the same amount of the same whole.
0.2 is a different amount, so the set is not equivalent.

vocabulary.definition: A way to compare a number to 100, shown with the % sign.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una manera de comparar un número con 100, con el signo %.
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio that compares a number to 100, written with a % sign, is a ___.

examples.text: 9 out of 100 students walk to school → 9%
examples.why: The comparison is already out of 100.
That is 90%, not 9% — both terms must be scaled to 100.

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número con un punto, como 0.5, que muestra una parte menor que uno.
vocabulary.cloze: A number that uses a point to show parts of a whole is a ___.

examples.why: The percent divided by 100 gives the decimal.
Multiplying by a plain 35 makes the answer 100 times too big.

vocabulary.definition: Having the same value, just written a different way.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tener el mismo valor, escrito de otra forma.
vocabulary.cloze: Having the same value but written a different way is being ___.

vocabulary.definition: A familiar number you use to guess, like 50% or 1/2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número conocido que usas para estimar, como 50% o 1/2.
vocabulary.cloze: A common, easy-to-remember value like 50% or 1/4 used for comparing is a ___.

examples.text: Using 25% of 80 to check a 24% discount
examples.why: A friendly percent close enough to estimate with.
Those are the exact numbers — that is computing, not benchmarking.

vocabulary.definition: Money taken off the first price to make it cheaper.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dinero que se quita del precio original para que sea más barato.
vocabulary.cloze: An amount taken off a price, often given as a percent, is a ___.

examples.why: Money taken off the original price.

examples.text: The $60 you pay at the register
examples.why: That is the sale price — what is left after the discount.

items.meaning: Three equivalent ways to name the same part of a whole
A way to compare a number to 100

steps: 1. Percent to Decimal: Divide by 100 (move decimal point 2 places left)
2. Decimal to Percent: Multiply by 100 (move decimal point 2 places right)
3. Fraction to Percent: Divide numerator by denominator, then convert decimal to percent

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Sleepy Animals
revealWordProblem.text:
The table shows the average total sleep time for different animals as a part of a 24-hour day. Some are written as decimals, some as fractions, and some as percents.
Question: How do the sleep times compare? Order the animals from the one that sleeps the most to the one that sleeps the least. Which animal's sleep time surprised you, and why?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A table of average sleep time as part of a 24-hour day for eight animals, written as a mix of decimals, fractions, and percents.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Rewrite every value in the same form — decimals are easiest. Python 3/4 = 0.75, Tiger 0.65, Cheetah 0.5, Duck 0.45, Chimpanzee 2/5 = 0.4, Human 33% = 0.33, Cow 16.5% = 0.165, Giraffe 8/100 = 0.08. From most to least: python, tiger, cheetah, duck, chimpanzee, human, cow, giraffe. The giraffe is the surprise — 0.08 of a day is only about 2 hours of sleep, while the python sleeps about 18.

reviewCheck.stem: A game shows your score as 7/8 complete. What percent is that?
reviewCheck.explanation: 8 does not scale to 100 by a whole number, so divide: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, and 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. That is 87.5 out of 100.
choiceFeedback: 8 will not scale to 100 evenly — divide 7 by 8, then multiply by 100.
Convert the fraction to a decimal first.
88% is the rounded version, but this score converts exactly. Divide 7 by 8 and keep every decimal place — the percent is not a whole number.
hints: Try the out-of-100 move first: is there a whole number you can multiply 8 by to get exactly 100?
There isn't (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), so use the backup method: divide the numerator by the denominator.
7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, which is 87.5/100 — slide the decimal two places right to read the percent.
reviewCheck.stemEs: Un juego muestra tu puntaje como 7/8 completado. ¿Qué porcentaje es eso?
reviewCheck.explanationEs: 8 no escala a 100 con un número entero, así que divide: 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, y 0.875 × 100 = 87.5%. Eso es 87.5 de cada 100.
hintsEs: Prueba primero el paso de cada 100: ¿hay un número entero por el que puedas multiplicar 8 para llegar exactamente a 100?
No lo hay (8 × 12 = 96, 8 × 13 = 104), así que usa el método de respaldo: divide el numerador entre el denominador.
7 ÷ 8 = 0.875, que es 87.5/100; desliza el punto dos lugares a la derecha para leer el porcentaje.
